astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ch.title: Two Ways to Burn Hydrogen

notes.title: Thermonuclear Reactions in Stars (The Sensitivity of the Rates to Temperature, eq. 4.65)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ch.topic: Log-log plot of eps_pp ∝ ρX²T⁴ and eps_CNO ∝ ρXZT²⁰ against central temperature, with Z and X sliders and a flashing core inset showing the CNO share.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ch.aha: A 10% rise in T multiplies the CNO rate nearly sevenfold but the p-p rate only by half, so the lines cross just above the Sun's central temperature.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-cl.title: A Star Cluster Growing Old

notes.title: Star Clusters and Their Ages (Isochrones and the Turn-Off Point, eqs. 4.80-4.81)
Stellar Evolution on and beyond the Main Sequence (The Main-Sequence Lifetime)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-cl.topic: HR diagram of 27 coeval stars with an age slider; stars peel off the main sequence as the turn-off moves down, with a lifetime-vs-mass inset.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-cl.aha: A 10 M☉ star with ten times the fuel lives about 300 times shorter than the Sun, so the turn-off sweeps down the main sequence and marks the cluster's age.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-co.title: Reading a Star's Temperature from Its Colour

notes.title: Magnitudes, Colours, and the Distance Ladder (Colour Index and Colour Temperature, eqs. 1.8-1.10, Fig. 3)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-co.topic: Black-body B−V colour index versus temperature, with the Wien form, a ±δ uncertainty band mapped onto an allowed temperature range, and a spectrum inset with B and V bands.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-co.aha: The same ±0.05 mag colour error that pins the Sun to ±4% leaves a 40 000 K star anywhere from about 28 000 to 76 000 K, because both bands sit on the Rayleigh-Jeans tail.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-cu.title: Adding Atoms to an Absorption Line

notes.title: Stellar Atmospheres and the Formation of Lines (equivalent width eq. 3.43, curve of growth, Fig. 36)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-cu.topic: Na D2 line profile through a cool layer and its equivalent width, traced onto the curve of growth (linear, flat, damping) as N, T and damping width vary.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-cu.aha: Once the core bottoms out, ten times more atoms barely widen the line, yet on the damping part W grows as √N again and stops caring about temperature.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-di.title: Nearby Stars in a Turning Galaxy

notes.title: The Milky Way (Differential Rotation; The Oort Constants, eqs. 7.9-7.11)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-di.topic: Face-on Galactic disc in the Sun's rotating frame: a ring of nearby stars coloured by radial velocity shows the sin 2l pattern, with flat/Keplerian/rigid rotation curves and Oort's A.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-di.aha: Stars moving at exactly the Sun's speed still recede toward l = 45° and 225° and approach at 135° and 315°, and the ring shears into an ellipse; rigid rotation turns every star grey.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-do.title: The 21-cm Line of a Tilted Disc

notes.title: Galaxies and Their Scaling Relations (The Tully-Fisher Relation: eqs. 8.9-8.10, Figs. 92-93)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-do.topic: An inclined rotating gas disc (i, vc, σ) builds its double-horned 21-cm profile; width W ≈ 2vc sin i, with cos i = b/a from the image and the inferred W/2 sin i.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-do.aha: A 200 km/s disc at 30° and a 100 km/s disc edge-on give the same line, and at i = 10° dividing by sin i inflates the inferred speed to about 240 km/s.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ec.title: An Eclipsing Binary

notes.title: Binary Stars and the Masses and Radii of Stars (Eclipsing Binaries: eq. 2.27, Fig. 15)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ec.topic: Edge-on circular binary of uniform discs with adjustable radii and temperatures; two eclipses traced on F/F0 with contact times ta-td and depths of both minima.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ec.aha: Both eclipses hide the same area πRs², so their depth ratio is exactly (Ts/Tl)⁴ whatever the radii, and the deeper one always hides the hotter star.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ev.title: The View from Another Galaxy

notes.title: The Expanding Universe (Hubble's law has no centre, Fig. 95; The Hubble Time, eq. 9.8)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ev.topic: Twenty galaxies obeying Hubble's law from A; click any galaxy to become the observer and see the velocity field and v-d plot recomputed, with d/v = 1/H0.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ev.aha: Click any galaxy, even one at the corner, and every other galaxy recedes radially from it on the same v = H0 d line: the expansion has no centre.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-fl.title: The Rotation of the Galaxy

notes.title: The Milky Way (The Flat Rotation Curve, eq. 7.15, Fig. 88)
The Evidence for Dark Matter (Flat Rotation Curves, eq. 9.13)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-fl.topic: Milky Way disc face-on with tracers vs 'ghost' stars-and-gas-only orbits, the rotation curve with and without a dark halo (with cut-off), and M(s) = s vc²/G and the dark share.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-fl.aha: With the halo on, the 35 kpc tracer turns nearly three times as far as its stars-only ghost in one solar orbit, and M(s) keeps doubling with radius where there is no light left.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ga.title: Which Pairs of Nuclei Fuse

notes.title: Thermonuclear Reactions in Stars (Tunnelling and the Gamow Factor; The Reaction Rate and the Gamow Peak, eqs. 4.57-4.58, 4.64, Fig. 50)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ga.topic: The Maxwell factor, the tunnelling factor and their product (Gamow peak) against E/kT for p+p, ³He+³He and p+¹⁴N, beside the Coulomb barrier with the turning point at E0.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ga.aha: Solar fusion happens at about 4.5 kT, which is still about 100 times below the Coulomb barrier, and for p+¹⁴N the peak moves out to 20 kT and becomes 20 orders of magnitude rarer.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-gr.title: Small Bodies Approaching a Growing Planet

notes.title: Exoplanets and the Formation of Planetary Systems (gravitational focusing, eqs. 2.40-2.44, Fig. 20; runaway growth)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-gr.topic: Exact two-body hyperbolae of planetesimals fired at a planet of variable mass and v∞; streams reveal b_max and the focusing factor σ/πR² = 1 + vesc²/v∞².
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-gr.aha: Bodies aimed more than twice the planet's radius away still hit it at v∞ = 6 km/s, and ten times the mass gives about fifteen times the cross-section: runaway growth.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ke.title: Finding a Body on Its Ellipse

notes.title: Kepler's Laws and Orbital Elements (The Eccentric Anomaly, Fig. 10; Kepler's equation 2.13; Solving Kepler's Equation 2.14-2.15)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ke.topic: An ellipse with its auxiliary circle: mean anomaly η, eccentric anomaly ψ, true anomaly θ and the swept area FPB, with θ(t) plotted against a circular orbit.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ke.aha: At e = 0.8 the body spends only about a twentieth of its period on the half of the orbit nearer the star.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ki.title: Three Spectra from One Gas

notes.title: Radiative Transfer (Emission and the Source Function, eqs. 3.29-3.30, Fig. 32)
Stellar Spectra and Their Classification (Kirchhoff's laws, Fig. 21)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ki.topic: A 6000 K source seen directly, through a Balmer-line hydrogen slab and the slab alone; gas temperature and line optical depth set S = B(Tgas) and I = I0 e^-τ + S(1−e^-τ).
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ki.aha: Heat the gas to the source's temperature and the absorption lines vanish; heat it further and the same slab in front of the star gives bright emission lines.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-li.title: The Lighthouse Model of a Pulsar

notes.title: Neutron Stars and Pulsars (Pulsars; the lighthouse model, Figs. 77-78)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-li.topic: A 3D neutron star with a dipole field and two beam cones at inclination α; the flux trace at viewing angle ζ shows one, two or no pulses per 1.34 s turn, with the sky fraction swept.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-li.aha: The same steadily shining star is pulsed once per turn, twice per turn, steady, or invisible depending only on where the observer stands, and the beams sweep only about a quarter of the sky.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-li.title: Across the Disc of a Star

notes.title: Stellar Atmospheres and the Formation of Lines (Limb Darkening, eq. 3.42, Fig. 35; Eddington-Barbier relation)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-li.topic: A line of sight at impact parameter b meets the surface at angle θ; Eddington-Barbier picks the layer τ = cos θ in a grey atmosphere, painting the limb-darkened face and I(θ)/I(0) = (2+3cos θ)/5.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-li.aha: The limb is dark not because light is absorbed on the way out but because a slanting line of sight stops at a higher, cooler layer, and τ = 2/3 at b/R = 0.745 is exactly T_eff.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ne.title: A Star Shining Without Fuel

notes.title: Hydrostatic Equilibrium and the Virial Theorem (virial theorem, mean temperature eq. 4.23, E_tot for general γ, Contraction and the Kelvin-Helmholtz Time Scale, Fig. 43)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ne.topic: A 1 M☉ uniform star radiating L☉ with no fuel contracts from 10 R☉; bars of E_th, E_grav and E_tot and readouts show it heating as it loses energy, for γ = 5/3, 3/2 and 1.4.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ne.aha: Switch on the radiation and the star gets hotter as it loses energy: at γ = 5/3 exactly half the released gravitational energy is radiated and half heats the gas, and at γ = 1.4 the gas gains five times what is radiated.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ob.title: Counting Photons from a Distant Star

notes.title: Telescopes, Detectors, and Observing across the Spectrum (photon rate eq. 1.19; The Signal-to-Noise Ratio, eqs. 1.21-1.22; seeing disc)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ob.topic: A star of given M_V at distance d observed with mirror D under a dark or moonlit sky; Poisson photon-by-photon detector image, S/N and the exposure needed for S/N = 10 against d.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ob.aha: Once the star is fainter than the sky in the seeing disc, the exposure time bends from t ∝ d² to t ∝ d⁴, and moonlight costs nothing for a bright star but a factor of 16 for a faint one.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ol.title: Lines of Sight Through a Field of Stars

notes.title: The Expanding Universe (Olbers' Paradox, eqs. 9.9-9.10, Fig. 97)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ol.topic: Lines of sight fired through random star fields fill a 20×20 patch of sky; mean path ℓ = 1/(nπR²), with an infinite universe versus a finite-age horizon ct0 that leaves 1 − e^(−ct0/ℓ) of the sky lit.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ol.aha: In an infinite universe every one of the 400 sightlines ends on a star, all equally bright, and only a horizon closer than ℓ darkens the sky; for the real universe the covered fraction is about 10⁻¹⁵.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-on.title: The Size of a Compact Star

notes.title: Degenerate Matter and White Dwarfs (energy minimisation, The Chandrasekhar Mass eq. 5.14, Fig. 71)
Neutron Stars and Pulsars (neutron-star radius eq. 5.30)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-on.topic: Radius at the energy minimum of a uniform degenerate sphere against mass, for electrons (any speed) and non-relativistic neutrons, drawn to scale beside the Earth or the Schwarzschild radius.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-on.aha: Doubling a white dwarf's mass shrinks it from 7250 to about 3960 km, and its radius plunges to zero near 1.72 M☉ as the electrons go ultra-relativistic; switch to neutrons and the same mass is a 10 km ball only about twice its Schwarzschild radius.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-on.title: A Distant Source Passing Behind a Point Mass

notes.title: The Evidence for Dark Matter (gravitational lensing: Einstein ring and radius, two images)
Dark Matter Candidates and Their Detection (microlensing, eqs. 9.32-9.34, Fig. 103)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-on.topic: A source drifting behind a point-mass lens: ray-shot images inside and outside the Einstein ring, and the achromatic magnification curve A(t) in blue and red, from a galaxy lens down to a stellar microlens.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-on.aha: The same point lens makes resolved arcs lasting tens of millions of years for a galaxy but an unresolved, colour-blind brightening lasting about a month for a star, with identical light curves in blue and red.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-pd.title: Placing Pulsars by Their Slowing Down

notes.title: Neutron Stars and Pulsars (characteristic age, magnetic field, P–Ṗ plane, Fig. 79)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-pd.topic: P–Ṗ plane with lines of constant t_char (slope +1) and constant B_p sin α (slope −1); place a pulsar, read age and field, spin it down at fixed field.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-pd.aha: A millisecond pulsar spinning eleven times faster than the Crab is about two million times older, and a constant-field pulsar slides down its slope −1 line through ever older ages.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-po.title: A Star Behind a Star

notes.title: The Evidence for Dark Matter (lens equation, Einstein ring, eq. 9.27–9.28)
Dark Matter Candidates and Their Detection (microlensing magnification)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-po.topic: Point-mass lens side view plus sky panel: two images θ± from θ² − βθ − θ_E² = 0, Einstein ring at β = 0, per-image and total magnification, source sliding behind the lens.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-po.aha: One star becomes two images on opposite sides of the lens, one inside and one outside the ring, and they turn into a full Einstein ring when the source is exactly behind.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-po.title: Stepping Out to the Surface of a Star

notes.title: Energy Transport and the Equations of Stellar Structure — Polytropes and the Lane–Emden Equation (eq. 4.39–4.42, Fig. 47)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-po.topic: Steps the Lane–Emden equation outward from the centre for n_p = 0…4, drawing w(ξ) and a density-shaded cross-section, with ξ₁ and ρ_c/ρ̄ at the surface and a same-radius density inset.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-po.aha: Rescaled to the same radius, the n_p = 3 star has only about 2 % of its central density halfway out, and ρ_c/ρ̄ jumps from 54 to more than 600 at n_p = 4.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-pr.title: Building Nuclei Beyond Iron

notes.title: The Nucleosynthesis of the Elements — s- and r-processes (Fig. 56)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-pr.topic: Chart of the nuclides (Mn–Se) with an Fe-56 seed in a neutron gas; a race clock compares t_cap = 1/(n_n σ v) with t_β, so the path either hugs the stable valley (s-process) or runs neutron-rich then decays at constant A (r-process).
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-pr.aha: The same seed follows the stable valley at 10^14 m^-3 but is driven far to the neutron-rich side at 10^27 m^-3, then everything cascades back along constant-A diagonals, exactly as in Fig. 56.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ra.title: Weighing the Stars of a Binary

notes.title: Binary Stars and the Masses and Radii of Stars — Spectroscopic Binaries (eq. 2.20–2.23, Fig. 13–14)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ra.topic: Double-lined spectroscopic binary: v_r curves of both stars about v_sys and a face-on orbit view; sliders for M1, M2, e, ω, i; readouts K1, K2 and M sin³i.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ra.aha: The heavier star swings less, raising M1 actually lowers K1, and an eccentric orbit turns the sinusoid into a sharp spike, whose shape flips with ω.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-sa.title: The Same Line in Two Stars

notes.title: Stellar Spectra and Their Classification — Luminosity Classes and pressure broadening
Stellar Atmospheres and the Formation of Lines (damping wings)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-sa.topic: Ca I 422.7 nm profile in a 5800 K dwarf and a giant of the same temperature: surface gravity g = GM/R² sets the pressure, and a Voigt line narrows in the giant.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-sa.aha: The giant, bigger and brighter, has the much narrower line (13 pm against 104 pm), and past a certain radius the width stops shrinking at the thermal core.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-sc.title: A Nudged Parcel of Gas

notes.title: Energy Transport — Convection and the Schwarzschild Criterion (eq. 4.32–4.33, Fig. 45)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-sc.topic: An adiabatic parcel nudged up by Δr in a layer of chosen |dT/dr| and γ; T against height for parcel (dashed) and surroundings (solid); the parcel oscillates back if stable or runs away if unstable.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-sc.aha: At 10 K/km the lifted parcel ends up 13 000 K cooler than its surroundings and swings back (buoyancy oscillation, P ≈ 86 min), while above 16 K/km, or with γ dropped to 1.2, it keeps rising.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-so.title: Counting the Sun's Neutrinos

notes.title: The Sun — solar neutrinos and the solar neutrino problem (eq. 4.75, Fig. 59)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-so.topic: Solar-neutrino spectrum (pp, pep, ⁷Be, CNO, ⁸B) with Ga/Cl/water thresholds; a cooler-core slider rescales each source by (T_c/T_c,0)^n and traces each detector's predicted rate against the measured fractions.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-so.aha: A 5 % cooler core cuts the water rate by more than two thirds but barely touches gallium, so no single temperature fits all three deficits, which forces new neutrino physics.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-st.title: Starlight through a Dust Cloud

notes.title: Gas, Dust, and the Phases of the Interstellar Medium — extinction, colour excess, R_V, correcting a distance (eq. 6.2–6.6)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-st.topic: B/V/red photons cross a dust cloud to a telescope; A_V, d and R_V sliders; readouts m_V, m_B − m_V and E(B−V); ghosts show where the star is placed with the dust ignored and after an R_V = 3.1 correction.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-st.aha: One magnitude of dust makes the star look 1.6 times farther away and redder, and the colour-excess correction brings it back, unless the dust's real R_V is not 3.1.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-st.title: Two Cores and a Burst of Energy

notes.title: Stellar Evolution — The Helium Flash and the Horizontal Branch
Hydrostatic Equilibrium and the Virial Theorem — negative heat capacity
Thermonuclear Reactions in Stars — ⟨σv⟩ ∝ T^ζ

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-st.topic: A helium core given an energy surge: an ideal-gas (virial, negative heat capacity) core dips and recovers, while a degenerate core heats and runs away; ζ = 4/20/40 sets the temperature sensitivity.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-st.aha: Adding energy to an ideal-gas core cools it, and it settles back to T0, while the same surge in a degenerate core with ζ = 40 runs away: the helium flash.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-st.title: A Hot Star in a Hydrogen Cloud

notes.title: Gas, Dust, and the Phases of the ISM — Strömgren sphere (eq. 6.12, Fig. 84)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-st.topic: Ionising photon rate and n_H set r_S = (3Ṅ/4πn_H²α)^(1/3); an animated Hα bubble with ionisation and recombination events, plus a neutral-fraction profile with a sharp edge.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-st.aha: The ionised region ends in a razor-sharp edge (about 5×10^-4 pc thick against a 3 pc radius), and a tenfold brighter star grows it by only a factor of 2.15.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-su.title: The Sun Seen from Every Planet

notes.title: Radiative Transfer — specific intensity constant along a ray
Galaxies and Their Scaling Relations — surface brightness independent of distance (eq. 8.1)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-su.topic: An observer flies from 0.35 to 32 AU: flux and solid angle both fall as 1/d², so F/Ω stays constant; an optional τ = 1 screen dims it.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-su.aha: From Neptune the Sun delivers 1/900 of the flux, yet every patch of its tiny disc looks exactly as bright as from Earth; only absorption changes that.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ta.title: Mapping the Galaxy's Rotation from Inside

notes.title: The Milky Way — The Rotation Curve and the Tangent-Point Method (eq. 7.12–7.13, Fig. 87)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ta.topic: Face-on disc with a line of sight at longitude l coloured by v_r; find v_r,max at the tangent point s0 sin l, add v0 sin l, and record points to build the rotation curve (flat or rising model).
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-ta.aha: Along a line of sight the fastest-receding gas is where the line grazes the circle s0 sin l, and adding v0 sin l recovers the true v_c, point by point, out to the solar circle only.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-tw.title: A Radio Interferometer of Two Dishes

notes.title: Telescopes, Detectors, and Observing — Radio Telescopes and Interferometry (eq. 1.23–1.24, Fig. 8)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-tw.topic: Two dishes and a drifting 21 cm source; the extra path ℓ sin θ; the receiver's mean power (Airy single-dish envelope × two-dish fringe factor) traced against θ, with baseline and dish-size sliders.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-tw.aha: As the source drifts, the power flickers through narrow fringes spaced λ/ℓ inside the broad single-dish hump, so the baseline and not the dish sets the resolution.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-we.title: Weighing an Unseen Companion

notes.title: Neutron Stars and Pulsars — black holes in binaries, mass function (eq. 5.41, Fig. 80, Problem 5)
Binary Stars — The Mass Function (eq. 2.25)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-we.topic: M2 against M1 for a fixed mass function f_m and inclination i (P = 6.5 d, V404 Cyg), traced curves for several i, a neutron-star mass band, and a face-on orbit with v_r arrows.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-we.aha: Whatever the visible star's mass or the tilt, the companion is never lighter than f_m, so an f_m of 6 M☉ proves a black hole.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-wh.title: How a White Dwarf Fades

notes.title: Degenerate Matter and White Dwarfs — The Cooling of White Dwarfs (eq. 5.15–5.19, Fig. 72)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-wh.topic: Mestel cooling of two 0.6 M☉ C white dwarfs born at different core temperatures: L(t) = L0(1 + t/t0)^(-7/5) on log–log axes with t0 ticks, the t^(-7/5) asymptote and the age of the Universe, plus to-scale discs beside the Earth.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-wh.aha: The white dwarf born four times hotter starts 128 times brighter, but after about 10^9 yr the two curves merge: the age of an old white dwarf forgets its birth temperature.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-wh.title: The Energy of a White Dwarf

notes.title: Degenerate Matter and White Dwarfs — uniform-sphere energy minimum and the Chandrasekhar Mass (eq. 5.10–5.14, Fig. 70)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-wh.topic: Per-electron E_K (dashed), E_grav (dotted) and total E (accent) against R for a uniform degenerate sphere; mass slider and non-relativistic/ultra-relativistic switch; the star drawn to scale beside the Earth.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-wh.aha: A heavier white dwarf is smaller, and in the ultra-relativistic limit the minimum disappears: above about 1.72 M☉ the star simply collapses.

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-wh.title: The Strength of the Balmer Lines

notes.title: The Boltzmann and Saha Equations — The Strength of the Balmer Lines (eq. 3.13, Fig. 27–28)

astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-wh.topic: Boltzmann n2/n_I (log) × Saha neutral fraction (linear) against T with electron-pressure control; the product peaks near 10^4 K, and the Balmer lines in a drawn spectrum darken and fade to match.
astrophysics and cosmology/courses/as-wh.aha: The excited fraction keeps rising steeply with temperature, yet the Balmer lines fade above about 10^4 K because the hydrogen is being ionised out from under them, so the lines peak in A stars.

electromagnetism/courses/em-amperian-loo.title: Amperian Loops Round Steady Currents

notes.title: Ampère's Law and the Curl of the Magnetic Field (circulation; long solenoid; toroid; plane current sheet)

electromagnetism/courses/em-amperian-loo.topic: Drag a circle/rectangle round a wire, three wires, solenoid rows, toroid or current sheet; plots B-parallel round the loop and compares the numerically summed circulation with mu0*I_enc.
electromagnetism/courses/em-amperian-loo.aha: The circulation stays at 12.57 uT m for a lopsided rectangle far off-centre round the wire, and is zero for the same rectangle moved beside it even though B is nonzero on every side.

electromagnetism/courses/em-bar-magnet-f.title: Three Fields Along a Bar Magnet

notes.title: Magnetisation and Bound Currents: A Uniformly Magnetised Cylinder
The Auxiliary Field and Linear Magnetic Materials (H_z(0) of the finite cylinder, eq. 6.29)

electromagnetism/courses/em-bar-magnet-f.topic: B_z, mu0 M_z and mu0 H_z on the axis of a uniformly magnetised cylinder vs z/a, with l/a from 0.2 to 8 and a probe that can straddle the end faces.
electromagnetism/courses/em-bar-magnet-f.aha: With no free current anywhere, H is not zero: it points against M inside (-0.03M for a rod, -0.90M for a thin disc) and jumps by M at each face while B is continuous.

electromagnetism/courses/em-capacitor-en.title: Charging a Capacitor a Little at a Time

notes.title: Conductors and Capacitance: The Energy Stored in a Capacitor
The Electrostatic Potential and Field Energy (u = 1/2 eps0 E^2)

electromagnetism/courses/em-capacitor-en.topic: Carries charge bead by bead across parallel plates or concentric spheres, building the V-q strips (W) and comparing with the integral of 1/2 eps0 E^2 over the gap.
electromagnetism/courses/em-capacitor-en.aha: The first bead crosses almost no potential difference, so the total work is 28.24 nJ = QV/2, and the field energy integral lands on exactly the same number.

electromagnetism/courses/em-changing-sol.title: A Solenoid with a Changing Current

notes.title: Faraday's Law and Lenz's Law: The Induced Electric Field / The Field of a Solenoid with a Changing Current

electromagnetism/courses/em-changing-sol.topic: End-on long solenoid with dI/dt; plots the induced E_phi against s inside (grows as s) and outside (falls as 1/s where B=0), with a Lenz ring.
electromagnetism/courses/em-changing-sol.aha: There is a circulating electric field at s = 8 or 12 cm where B is exactly zero, set only by the total changing flux.

electromagnetism/courses/em-conduction-d.title: The Path of a Conduction Electron

notes.title: Current Density, Conductivity, and Ohm's Law: A Model of Conduction in a Metal (Figure 34, eqs 4.15-4.17)

electromagnetism/courses/em-conduction-d.topic: One electron's zigzag with and without a field on the same random sequence, plus the mean velocity of 20 000 electrons rising to the drift velocity -e E tau_c/m_e.
electromagnetism/courses/em-conduction-d.aha: The field-on path always ends to the left of its field-off twin (opposite E) even though each run's zigzag goes anywhere, and the mean velocity settles within a few tau_c at a value proportional to E.

electromagnetism/courses/em-disc-field-a.title: The Field of a Disc, Ring by Ring

notes.title: Coulomb's Law and the Electric Field: The Field of a Disc on Its Axis (Figure 6, eqs 1.17-1.21)

electromagnetism/courses/em-disc-field-a.topic: Builds E_z on the axis of a charged disc ring by ring, with the running total, angle theta at P, and E_z vs z for discs of 3/10/30 cm and the infinite plane.
electromagnetism/courses/em-disc-field-a.aha: For the infinite plane the field at 10 cm is the same 5.65e4 N/C as at 5 cm, and the rings within 45 deg supply the same share at either height.

electromagnetism/courses/em-divergence-s.title: Flux out of a Small Box

notes.title: Electric Flux and Gauss's Law: The Divergence / The Divergence Theorem

electromagnetism/courses/em-divergence-s.topic: Face-by-face flux out of a small cube in kappa*r, uniform, point-charge and charged-ball fields, with Phi/l^3 plotted as the cube shrinks.
electromagnetism/courses/em-divergence-s.aha: Next to a point charge every arrow points outward, yet the net flux per volume is zero; only where there is charge (or in kappa*r) does it stay finite as the cube shrinks.

electromagnetism/courses/em-field-line-b.title: Field Lines Crossing a Slab

notes.title: Maxwell's Equations in Matter: The Bending of Field Lines / A Dielectric Slab in a Uniform Field (Figure 89, eq. 8.43)

electromagnetism/courses/em-field-line-b.topic: Uniform E or B crossing a linear slab at beta_0: lines refract with tan beta = eps_r (or mu_r) tan beta_0, E lines end on bound charge, B lines are continuous and crowd together.
electromagnetism/courses/em-field-line-b.aha: E and B lines both bend away from the normal (unlike light), but three E lines in four stop on bound charge while every B line carries on and crowds together.

electromagnetism/courses/em-filled-capac.title: Filling a Capacitor with a Dielectric

notes.title: The Electric Displacement and Linear Dielectrics: the filled parallel-plate capacitor (eqs 3.31-3.34)

electromagnetism/courses/em-filled-capac.topic: Edge-on capacitor with free charge, bound layers on the dielectric, D and E arrows and a pillbox, for isolated plates or a 100 V battery as eps_r goes 1 to 4.
electromagnetism/courses/em-filled-capac.aha: With the plates isolated D stays at 0.885 uC/m^2 while E and V drop by eps_r; with a battery the extra free charge exactly equals the bound layer that appears next to it.

electromagnetism/courses/em-gauss-cones..title: Narrow Cones through a Closed Surface

notes.title: Electric Flux and Gauss's Law: The Solid Angle and the proof of Gauss's law (Figure 8)

electromagnetism/courses/em-gauss-cones..topic: Narrow cones from charges cut patches on dented, C- and E-shaped closed surfaces; each patch flux is shown, crossings are counted in a sweep, and the total flux is Q_enc/eps0.
electromagnetism/courses/em-gauss-cones..aha: The patch flux is the same 0.155 V m whether the cone meets the surface near or far, and a cone that crosses a folded surface three times still nets exactly one outward crossing.

electromagnetism/courses/em-lc-spring-tw.title: The LC Circuit and Its Spring Twin

notes.title: Phasors and Complex Impedance: The LC Circuit (eqs 7.56-7.59, Figure 74)

electromagnetism/courses/em-lc-spring-tw.topic: Ideal LC loop released with Q0 = 1 mC, energy bar split electric/magnetic, and a mass-on-spring twin with m <-> L, kappa <-> 1/C; Q and I traces.
electromagnetism/courses/em-lc-spring-tw.aha: When the capacitor is empty the current is at its largest, just as the block is fastest at x = 0, and the energy passes between C and L twice per period.

electromagnetism/courses/em-lcr-discharg.title: Capacitor Discharge through L and R

notes.title: Phasors and Complex Impedance: The Damped LCR Circuit (eqs 7.60-7.62, Figure 75)

electromagnetism/courses/em-lcr-discharg.topic: Series LCR discharge from Q0 = 10 uC with R 0-800 ohm and C 0.25/1/4 uF; Q(t) with envelope, earlier runs in grey, energy bookkeeping including heat in R.
electromagnetism/courses/em-lcr-discharg.aha: Raising R past 2 sqrt(L/C) = 200 ohm stops the overshoot, and going further to 800 ohm makes the discharge slower, not faster.

electromagnetism/courses/em-lcr-phasor-d.title: The Phasor Diagram of a Driven LCR Circuit

notes.title: Resonance and Power in Alternating-Current Circuits: The Driven Series LCR Circuit (Figure 79, eqs 7.73-7.75)
Phasors and Complex Impedance

electromagnetism/courses/em-lcr-phasor-d.topic: Phasor diagram of a driven series LCR: I along the real axis, V_R, V_L, V_C head to tail summing to the 10 V source phasor, psi vs omega, rotating projections for V(t) and I(t).
electromagnetism/courses/em-lcr-phasor-d.aha: The three component amplitudes add to 18.9 V yet the source is only 10 V, and psi flips sign as omega passes 1/sqrt(LC).

electromagnetism/courses/em-lcr-resonanc.title: Potential Differences in a Driven LCR Circuit

notes.title: Resonance and Power in Alternating-Current Circuits
Problems 1-2 (V_C peak below ω0; V_L=V_C=𝒬V0 at resonance)

electromagnetism/courses/em-lcr-resonanc.topic: Peak voltmeter reading across R, L, C and L+C of a driven series LCR circuit swept in ω, at Q = 5, 2, 1.
electromagnetism/courses/em-lcr-resonanc.aha: A 1 V source puts 5 V across the capacitor and 5 V across the inductor, yet the meter across L and C together reads zero.

electromagnetism/courses/em-line-integra.title: The Line Integral near a Point Charge

notes.title: The Electrostatic Potential and Field Energy: The Line Integral of the Field (Figure 12)
The curl test and the field κ(0,x,0)

electromagnetism/courses/em-line-integra.topic: Running sum of E·dℓ along draggable paths from A to B near a point charge (straight, arch, far side, closed loop), plotted against r, plus the non-conservative field κ(0,x,0).
electromagnetism/courses/em-line-integra.aha: A path that heads towards the charge first drives the running sum negative (−117 V) and still ends at exactly 300 V, and every path retraces the same curve against r, while the κ(0,x,0) loop gives +188 V.

electromagnetism/courses/em-magnetic-fie.title: The Magnetic Field between the Plates of a Capacitor

notes.title: The Displacement Current and Maxwell's Equations: The Magnetic Field between the Plates (Figure 83)

electromagnetism/courses/em-magnetic-fie.topic: B on a probe circle of radius s in the midplane of a charging disc capacitor from the Ampère–Maxwell law, B vs s compared with the wire's μ0I/2πs.
electromagnetism/courses/em-magnetic-fie.aha: With no charge crossing the gap there is still a B field between the plates, rising linearly to the edge and then landing exactly on the wire's curve; switch the current off and B vanishes although E is still there.

electromagnetism/courses/em-magnetised-s.title: A Magnetised Slab Cut into Current Loops

notes.title: Magnetisation and Bound Currents (Figures 54-55, slab cut into blocks)

electromagnetism/courses/em-magnetised-s.topic: A magnetised slab cut into 5×4 to 20×16 block current loops; net current on shared and rim edges, for uniform M and for a gradient ∂Mz/∂y.
electromagnetism/courses/em-magnetised-s.aha: Cutting the slab finer never changes the rim current (K_b = M = 1000 A/m), and with a gradient the edge currents shrink as Δy while K/Δy stays at G: J_b = ∇×M emerges as a limit on screen.

electromagnetism/courses/em-one-loop-two.title: One Loop and Two Surfaces

notes.title: The Displacement Current and Maxwell's Equations: Ampère's Law and a Charging Capacitor (Figure 82)

electromagnetism/courses/em-one-loop-two.topic: Fixed Ampère loop round a capacitor's charging wire; the surface is deformed from the flat disc S1 into a bag S2 through the gap, with and without Maxwell's displacement term.
electromagnetism/courses/em-one-loop-two.aha: Moving an imaginary surface makes μ0I_enc drop to zero while the circulation does not change, and switching on ε0dΦE/dt makes the right-hand side flat at 1.26 μT·m for all thirteen surfaces, independent of plate area.

electromagnetism/courses/em-paddle-wheel.title: The Paddle Wheel and the Curl

notes.title: Ampère's Law and the Curl of the Magnetic Field: The Curl; Ampère's Law in Differential Form

electromagnetism/courses/em-paddle-wheel.topic: A small loop/paddle wheel dragged through a rigidly rotating fluid and the field of a thick wire; arc contributions, circulation/area vs s.
electromagnetism/courses/em-paddle-wheel.aha: The wire's field lines are circles, yet outside the wire the paddle wheel does not turn at all (arcs +0.200 and −0.200 cancel), while inside the wire it turns exactly like the rotating fluid.

electromagnetism/courses/em-polarisation.title: The Tip of the Electric Field

notes.title: Polarisation, Energy Flux, and Radiation Pressure: Circular and Elliptical Polarisation (Figure 94)

electromagnetism/courses/em-polarisation.topic: Path of the tip of E at z = 0 for Ex = E1 cos ωt, Ey = E2 cos(ωt − ψ); linear, circular and elliptical polarisation with tilt and sense readouts.
electromagnetism/courses/em-polarisation.aha: ψ = 3π/4 gives exactly the ψ = π/4 ellipse tilted the other way but still anticlockwise: the sign of sin ψ sets the sense, cos ψ the tilt.

electromagnetism/courses/em-rc-rl-switch.title: Switching a Capacitor and an Inductor

notes.title: Transients in RC and RL Circuits: Discharging/Charging a Capacitor (Figure 38)
Growth and decay of current in an RL circuit

electromagnetism/courses/em-rc-rl-switch.topic: Two-way switch S connecting R with C or an ideal L to a 6 V source (position 1) or across each other (position 2); I and V traces with tangent-to-final-value construction.
electromagnetism/courses/em-rc-rl-switch.aha: At a throw the capacitor's current jumps while the inductor's voltage jumps, and raising R slows the capacitor (τ = RC) but speeds up the inductor (τ = L/R).

electromagnetism/courses/em-ring-or-magn.title: Moving the Ring or Moving the Magnet

notes.title: Faraday's Law and Lenz's Law: The Induced Electric Field
The Motional Electromotive Force

electromagnetism/courses/em-ring-or-magn.topic: Ring slid over a magnet vs magnet moved through a ring at the same relative speed: flux and emf traces, magnetic vs electric force per unit charge, and a wire-free dashed loop.
electromagnetism/courses/em-ring-or-magn.aha: The emf traces are identical, but in one run v×B does the pushing and in the other an electric field does — and that electric field circulates even round an empty loop with no wire.

electromagnetism/courses/em-rod-on-rails.title: Pulling a Rod along Rails

notes.title: Faraday's Law and Lenz's Law: The Motional Electromotive Force (Figure 62, eq. 7.10-7.12)
The Motional Electromotive Force (school)

electromagnetism/courses/em-rod-on-rails.topic: Rod pulled at constant v along rails in B out of the page: ℰ = Bℓv, I, retarding force BIℓ, agent power = I²R, and a magnified charge showing v, v_d and the two magnetic-force parts.
electromagnetism/courses/em-rod-on-rails.aha: The total magnetic force on a charge in the rod is exactly perpendicular to its total velocity, so it does no work; the agent pulling the rod supplies every joule of heat.

mathematical methods/courses/ma-alembert.title: D'Alembert's Solution for a Released String

notes.title: The Classical Equations of Physics: D'Alembert's Solution of the Wave Equation (eq 7.8, Figure 60)

mathematical methods/courses/ma-alembert.topic: A string released from rest in a hump, triangle or rectangle splits into two half-height copies ½u0(x∓vt), with an x–t displacement map.
mathematical methods/courses/ma-alembert.aha: The released hump does not move off as a whole; it splits into two half-height copies, and the rectangle gives a stepped shape while the two halves still overlap.

mathematical methods/courses/ma-central-.title: Adding Up Random Numbers

notes.title: Probability and Random Variables: The Central Limit Theorem (eq 8.18, Figure 73)

mathematical methods/courses/ma-central-.topic: The exact density of the standardised sum of N uniform or exponential variables (computed by repeated convolution) against the standard Gaussian, with a largest-gap marker.
mathematical methods/courses/ma-central-.aha: Three uniform numbers already give an almost Gaussian bell, while a skewed exponential parent keeps a visible lean well past N = 10.

mathematical methods/courses/ma-convolut.title: Sliding One Pulse across Another

notes.title: Fourier Transforms and Convolution: Convolution (eq 6.33, Figure 54)

mathematical methods/courses/ma-convolut.topic: The reflected, shifted pulse slides across Π(x′); the grey overlap length is traced out as (Π∗Π)(x), plus the averaging window Π/2w option.
mathematical methods/courses/ma-convolut.aha: The value at each shift is just the length of the grey overlap, so the output is a triangle of height 2w and base 4w that falls linearly, not abruptly.

mathematical methods/courses/ma-cooling-.title: The Cooling of a Bar

notes.title: Separation of Variables in Cartesian Coordinates: The Cooling of a Bar (eqs 7.23-7.27)

mathematical methods/courses/ma-cooling-.topic: Separated sine-series solution of the diffusion equation for a bar with fixed end temperatures; uniform or jagged initial profile, log clock, per-mode decay stems.
mathematical methods/courses/ma-cooling-.aha: The jagged fine detail disappears within seconds while the overall hump takes about 1000 s, because mode n decays n² times faster; meanwhile the middle of the bar stays at 100 °C long after the ends have cooled.

mathematical methods/courses/ma-curl-pad.title: A Paddle Wheel in Three Flows

notes.title: Gradient, Divergence, and Curl: meaning of the curl (eq 3.15, Figure 21)

mathematical methods/courses/ma-curl-pad.topic: A paddle wheel and two crossed fluid lines carried by the exact flow map in source, rotation and shear flows, with the angle turned plotted against t.
mathematical methods/courses/ma-curl-pad.aha: In the shear flow, where every streamline is straight, the wheel still turns clockwise at k/2, and at the centre of the rotation it spins in place at the same rate as anywhere else.

mathematical methods/courses/ma-heat-ker.title: A Flash of Heat in a Long Bar

notes.title: The Diffusion Equation on an Infinite Line: heat kernel (eqs 7.58-7.59, Figure 68)

mathematical methods/courses/ma-heat-ker.topic: The spreading Gaussian T(x,t) after a flash in a thin slice, with ±σ bar, ×4-time button, Figure 68 overlays, a distant thermometer and its reading against time.
mathematical methods/courses/ma-heat-ker.aha: Each time t is multiplied by four the curve gets twice as wide and half as tall with the area fixed, and a thermometer 16 cm away is already warmed (by about 10⁻²⁷ K) after 1 s, so diffusion has no finite speed.

mathematical methods/courses/ma-hunting-.title: Hunting for Eigenvectors

notes.title: Eigenvalues, Diagonalisation, and Normal Modes: Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors (eqs 4.30-4.32; rotation and shear examples)

mathematical methods/courses/ma-hunting-.topic: A unit vector x swept round the circle with its image Ax; eigen-directions light up where the turning angle α crosses zero, for a symmetric matrix, a rotation and the shear.
mathematical methods/courses/ma-hunting-.aha: A sweep finds two perpendicular lines for the symmetric matrix, none at all for a rotation (the complex eigenvalues), and only one for the shear, where α touches zero without crossing.

mathematical methods/courses/ma-newton-r.title: Following the Tangent to a Root

notes.title: Root Finding, Interpolation, and Linear Systems: The Newton–Raphson Method (Figure 81, eq 9.18 onwards)

mathematical methods/courses/ma-newton-r.topic: Newton–Raphson tangents followed to the axis for x²−C, (x−√C)², sgn(x)√|x| and ∛x, with correct digits −log10|e_n| plotted against n.
mathematical methods/courses/ma-newton-r.aha: The correct digits double every step for a simple root but crawl up by 0.3 digits per step for a double root, while √|x| bounces between ±x0 for ever and ∛x runs away, doubling each step.

mathematical methods/courses/ma-one-recu.title: One Recurrence, Two Directions

notes.title: Root Finding, Interpolation, and Linear Systems: The Stability of an Algorithm (eqs 9.11-9.14)

mathematical methods/courses/ma-one-recu.topic: J_n = 1 − nJ_{n−1} run forwards from J0 = 1−1/e (with optional added ε_m errors) or backwards from a crude guess, with values in the true band and |Δ_n| on a log scale.
mathematical methods/courses/ma-one-recu.aha: An exact formula fed an error of only 10⁻¹⁷ blows up into alternating nonsense by n = 18 because the error grows as n!, while the same relation run backwards from the crude guess 0 converges to full precision.

mathematical methods/courses/ma-plucked-.title: Building a Plucked String from Its Normal Modes

notes.title: Separation of Variables in Cartesian Coordinates: the plucked string (eqs 7.20-7.22)

mathematical methods/courses/ma-plucked-.topic: A plucked string as the sum of its first M normal modes, with rows n = 1-6 magnified by n², amplitude stems |A_n|, adjustable pluck point and time.
mathematical methods/courses/ma-plucked-.aha: Plucking at the middle removes every even mode, and plucking at L/3 removes modes 3 and 6, because a mode with a node at the pluck point cannot help build the corner there.

mathematical methods/courses/ma-precisio.title: Choosing the Step Size

notes.title: Numerical Differentiation and Quadrature — Choosing the Step Size (eqs 9.37–9.38, Fig. 85)
Floating-Point Arithmetic (mantissa t, ε_m)

mathematical methods/courses/ma-precisio.topic: Error |D − e| of forward/central/Richardson difference derivatives of e^x at x=1 against h on log–log axes, with f rounded to a t-bit mantissa; truncation Ah^p, round-off Bε_m/h and h_opt bounds.
mathematical methods/courses/ma-precisio.aha: Sweeping h downward, the error falls along a straight line and then climbs raggedly back up — below ~1e-8 the computed derivative is exactly 0 — so a smaller step makes the answer worse.

mathematical methods/courses/ma-radiatio.title: The Radiation Monitor at the Lab Door

notes.title: Probability and Random Variables — Bayes’s theorem, radiation monitor example (eq. 8.7)

mathematical methods/courses/ma-radiatio.topic: People walk through a monitor arch; carriers (fraction r) trip it with probability η1, others with η0; the running fraction of alarms from a source converges on P(R|G) = η1 r/[η1 r + η0(1−r)].
mathematical methods/courses/ma-radiatio.aha: A detector that catches 99% of sources is right only about one time in six when it sounds, because the 5% false-alarm rate acts on the 99% who carry nothing.

mathematical methods/courses/ma-radius-c.title: Partial Sums of the Logarithm Series

notes.title: Series, Limits, and Convergence — power series and radius of convergence, ln(1+x) example

mathematical methods/courses/ma-radius-c.topic: Partial sums S_N(x) of x − x²/2 + x³/3 − … against ln(1+x), with a probe and an error-vs-N inset; interval of convergence −1 < x ≤ 1 shaded.
mathematical methods/courses/ma-radius-c.aha: At x = 1.5 or 2, where ln(1+x) is perfectly smooth, adding more terms makes the sum swing further away — the radius is set by the singularity at x = −1.

mathematical methods/courses/ma-runge-ph.title: A Polynomial through Equally Spaced Points

notes.title: Root Finding, Interpolation, and Linear Systems — interpolation error and Runge’s phenomenon (Fig. 83)

mathematical methods/courses/ma-runge-ph.topic: Interpolating polynomial through N+1 equally spaced nodes of the bell 1/(1+x²/β²), with error curve and node-polynomial w(x) inset; largest error on [−1,1] and on the middle half.
mathematical methods/courses/ma-runge-ph.aha: Forcing the polynomial through more points of a narrow bell makes it worse — the error near the ends roughly doubles with each step of degree while the middle keeps improving.

mathematical methods/courses/ma-same-pul.title: One Pulse, Two Equations

notes.title: The Classical Equations of Physics — wave equation, d’Alembert’s solution
Separation of Variables in Polar and Spherical — diffusion on an infinite line, heat kernel (eqs 7.58–7.59)

mathematical methods/courses/ma-same-pul.topic: The same rectangular/triangular pulse evolved by the wave equation (d’Alembert, speed v) and by the heat equation (heat-kernel convolution); a probe reads both on a log scale down to 1e-16 and beyond.
mathematical methods/courses/ma-same-pul.aha: Half a second in, the rod two metres away is already warmer by 2.5×10⁻¹⁵ while the string is exactly flat — heat is felt everywhere at once, the wave only after a definite arrival time.

mathematical methods/courses/ma-square-w.title: Building a Square Wave from Sines

notes.title: Fourier Series — square-wave series (eq. 6.7, Fig. 48), Dirichlet’s theorem and the Gibbs phenomenon

mathematical methods/courses/ma-square-w.topic: Partial sums of the square-wave Fourier series (up to 50 non-zero terms) with a zoom on the jump, overshoot % and peak distance readouts, and a probe.
mathematical methods/courses/ma-square-w.aha: The overshoot beside the jump refuses to shrink — it stays near 9% of the jump while sliding closer as L/(2N) — yet at any fixed x the sum still converges.

mathematical methods/courses/ma-terms-th.title: Adding Up Smaller and Smaller Terms

notes.title: Series, Limits, and Convergence — the harmonic series vs Σ1/n² (Fig. 1, Fig. 2)

mathematical methods/courses/ma-terms-th.topic: Stems 1/n with partial sums of 1/n and 1/n², on a linear axis to 20 and a log axis to 1000, with π²/6 marked.
mathematical methods/courses/ma-terms-th.aha: On the log axis the harmonic sums rise in a dead-straight line — about 0.69 per doubling forever — while the 1/n² sums flatten onto π²/6.

mathematical methods/courses/ma-two-mass.title: Two Masses on Three Springs

notes.title: Eigenvalues, Diagonalisation, and Normal Modes — two masses and three springs (Fig. 42)

mathematical methods/courses/ma-two-mass.topic: Two blocks between walls on springs k, k′, k; in-phase, antiphase or first-block-only starts, x1, x2 against t, normal coordinates q1, q2 and mode frequencies.
mathematical methods/courses/ma-two-mass.aha: Start either normal-mode shape and it keeps that shape forever; start one block alone and with a weak middle spring the motion passes completely to the other block and back.

mathematical methods/courses/ma-why-outw.title: A Small Box in Spherical Coordinates

notes.title: Curvilinear Coordinates — divergence in curvilinear coordinates, ∇·r̂ = 2/r (eq. 3.72)
Gradient, Divergence, and Curl — divergence as flux from a small box

mathematical methods/courses/ma-why-outw.topic: A small spherical-coordinate box in the field r̂, r̂/r² or r; face fluxes by quadrature and Φ/V against Δr tending to the divergence.
mathematical methods/courses/ma-why-outw.aha: The field r̂ has the same size everywhere, yet four times as much flux leaves the outer face as enters the inner one, so its divergence is 2/r, not 0.

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.title: The Carnot Cycle of an Ideal Gas

notes.title: Heat Engines and the Carnot Cycle (The Carnot Cycle, Fig. 11, eqs 2.28–2.31)
Entropy (The Carnot Cycle on the Temperature–Entropy Plane, Fig. 17)

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.topic: Carnot cycle of 1 mol ideal gas on p–V and T–S planes; sliders for T_h, T_c, V_B/V_A and γ, with Q_h, Q_c, W_by and η readouts.
thermal and statistical physics/courses/.aha: Switching monatomic to diatomic makes the loop visibly longer and thinner but the work and efficiency don't budge — and lowering T_c by 100 K beats raising T_h by 100 K.

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.title: Carnot's Theorem: Engine Meets Heat Pump

notes.title: Heat Engines and the Carnot Cycle (Carnot's Theorem, Fig. 12)
The Kelvin and Clausius Statements

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.topic: A claimed engine X drives a reversible R backwards (Fig. 12 bookkeeping); energy-flow arrows and net-result bars show when the pair violates the Kelvin statement.
thermal and statistical physics/courses/.aha: Dial η_X above 1 − T_c/T_h and the pair visibly turns cold-reservoir heat alone into work with the hot reservoir untouched — the Kelvin violation appears as bars, and it vanishes exactly at the Carnot efficiency.

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.title: The Chemical Potential of a Liquid and Its Vapour

notes.title: Phase Coexistence (Equilibrium Between Two Phases; The Chemical Potential of Each Phase, Fig. 42, eq. 6.4)

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.topic: μ_liq and μ_gas of water vs T at adjustable pressure; crossing T_0, slopes −s, pressure shifts v Δp, boiling point on Everest.
thermal and statistical physics/courses/.aha: Raising p lifts the gas line ~22 meV while the liquid line moves 0.02 meV, so the crossing — the boiling point — slides; at Everest pressure water boils at 71 °C.

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.title: The Slopes of a Phase Diagram

notes.title: Phase Coexistence (The Clausius–Clapeyron Equation, eqs 6.5–6.9, Fig. 41)
Problems §6.1 nos. 1–2 (sublimation vs vaporisation slope; water's melting curve)

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.topic: p/p_t vs T/T_t phase diagram built from dp/dT = L/(TΔV) on all three coexistence curves; sliders for ℓ_fus and Δv_fus (through zero to negative, water-like).
thermal and statistical physics/courses/.aha: Sliding Δv_fus through zero makes the melting line stand vertical and then lean left — the water anomaly — and doubling L is indistinguishable from halving ΔV.

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.title: Tangents to the Gibbs Curve of a Mixture

notes.title: Mixtures and Phase Separation (The Chemical Potentials of a Mixture, Fig. 45, eqs 6.31–6.32)
Mixtures and Phase Separation (The Common Tangent, Fig. 46, eqs 6.33–6.35)

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.topic: Draggable tangent to g(x) of the random-arrangement lattice model (k_BT = 0.35ε) reading μ_A, μ_B as intercepts; common tangent, lever-rule phase fractions, tilt τx.
thermal and statistical physics/courses/.aha: The coexisting phases are NOT the two well bottoms — the tangent only touches twice just to their right — and sweeping the overall composition leaves the two phase compositions fixed while only the amounts change.

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.title: Counting Molecules in Half a Vessel

notes.title: Probability for Many Particles (binomial distribution, left/right half of vessel, Fig. 25)

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.topic: Live snapshots of N = 25, 100, 400 molecules counted in the left half (or fifth) against the exact binomial N·P(n) vs n/N; spread and relative width measured.
thermal and statistical physics/courses/.aha: The spread of the count grows (2.5 → 5 → 10) while the relative width shrinks (0.2 → 0.1 → 0.05) — extrapolate to a litre of air and the fluctuation is 6 × 10⁻¹².

Photons and Blackbody Radiation (The Stefan–Boltzmann Law)

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.aha: Under equipartition the running total grows as ω_c³ off the chart (the ultraviolet catastrophe); switch to quantised modes and it flattens at the Stefan–Boltzmann value, rising as T⁴ because the number of thawed modes grows as T³.

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.aha: The free expansion takes in no heat at all, yet the gas's entropy bar rises by exactly the same 5.76 J/K as in the reversible run — entropy belongs to the end state, and the gap ∫δQ/T < ΔS is the Clausius inequality.

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.aha: The staircase of W_by creeps up towards −ΔF as the steps multiply but never passes it, and the shaded gap between staircase and isotherm is exactly T S_gen — lost work made visible.

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.title: Two Samples and a Partition

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.aha: ΔS/Nk_B is 0.693 for argon-38 exactly as for helium or krypton, and 0 only for argon-40 — and the labelled count makes the entropy of an isolated vessel fall when the partition is slid back in.

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.title: Isotherm and Adiabat through the Same State

notes.title: Functions of State and the First Law (first law dU = δQ + δW, reversible adiabat TV^(γ−1) and pV^γ constant)

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.aha: Same state, same slow piston: in the bath all 69.3 J of work leaves as heat, but insulated it all stays as internal energy — so the gas heats to 476 K, pushes back harder, needs 88.1 J, and the adiabat is exactly γ times steeper at C.

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.aha: The bar ends lie on a straight line on the log scale (÷1.25 per 2 km, no top edge), and doubling T halves n(0) while p(0) — the weight of the column — doesn't move at all.

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.title: A Curve Labelled by Its Slope: The Legendre Transform

notes.title: The Thermodynamic Potentials (Legendre transform eqs 3.4–3.9, Fig. 18)

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.aha: Shift the parabola sideways and the height-at-slope trace h(s) lands exactly on its old copy — it has forgotten where the curve was — while the intercept g(s) moves, and its tangents alone rebuild the curve in the right place.

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.title: The Mean Free Path of a Molecule

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.aha: The measured nσλ settles on 1 when the other molecules are frozen and drops to 1/√2 the moment they move, and the flight view shows the struck molecule usually came from outside the swept cylinder.

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.title: Two Species on a Lattice: the Gibbs Function of Mixing

notes.title: Mixtures and Phase Separation (The Free Energy of Mixing; Why a Trace of Anything Dissolves in Anything; The Common Tangent)

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.topic: Δg_mix(x) = εx(1−x) + kT[x ln x + (1−x) ln(1−x)] with energy/entropy parts, kT/ε slider, log-x slope inset, common tangent below kT = ε/2.
thermal and statistical physics/courses/.aha: Lowering kT through ε/2 turns the single bowl into a hump with two minima, and the log-x inset shows that even at kT = 0.1ε the slope is negative near x = 0, so a trace of B always dissolves (x_min ≈ e^(−ε/kT)).

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.title: Molecules on a Surface: occupied sites against chemical potential

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.aha: The spread of N at μ = −ε stays at √(M/4) whatever the temperature, while the band of μ with large scatter widens with T, and N/M scatter shrinks as 1/√M.

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.title: Adding Energy to Isolated Spins

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.aha: Past the top of the dome T jumps from +∞ to −∞ while β slides smoothly through zero, and moments at −0.97 K pour energy into a 1000 K block, so negative temperatures are hotter than every positive one.

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.title: One Oscillator and a Reservoir

The Einstein Solid (reservoir multiplicity, eq 5.37)

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.aha: As the reservoir grows the ratio p_(i+1)/p_i becomes the same for every level and the log plot straightens into the Boltzmann line, while a small reservoir's high levels sag below it because it cools as it gives up energy.

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.title: Removing the Partition: Counting the Arrangements of a Gas

Probability for Many Particles (Independent Objects with Two States; The Relative Width, eq 4.4)

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.aha: With 2 molecules a quarter of the looks find the gas back in the left half and S/k_B drops to 0, yet with 20 it would take about six days of looking, and at 10 000 the fraction just jitters by ±0.005 about one half.

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.title: A Crowd of Random Walkers

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.aha: Four times the time only doubles the rms distance while the steady walker goes four times as far, and doubling both ℓ and τ (same speed ℓ/τ) still makes the crowd spread faster, because what matters is ℓ²/τ.

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.title: Two Systems Dividing Their Energy

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.aha: At N1 = N2 = 10^6 the peak collapses to a line and the traces lie flat though energy still crosses the wall, while a 10-particle system touching a 10^6 one keeps its full ~1/√N1 wander.

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.title: Shearing a Gas between Two Plates

Transport in Gases (How Well the Argument Works - range of validity when λ exceeds the container)

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.topic: Air sheared between a fixed and a 1 m/s plate; drift profile with 2λ/3 brackets at the midplane, drag τ = J m Δu vs pressure 0.1 Pa-100 kPa for gaps 0.1/1/10 mm.
thermal and statistical physics/courses/.aha: Thinning the air a hundredfold leaves the drag at ~12 mPa because J falls 100× while each crosser's Δu grows 100×, until λ outgrows the gap and the drag then falls in proportion to p.

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.aha: Air at 300 K has λ_th 180 times smaller than the spacing, liquid helium's squares touch (Nλ³/V ≈ 1.5), and electrons in copper give ~7000, mostly because of their tiny mass rather than their density.

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.title: Two Einstein Solids Sharing Quanta

notes.title: Microstates, Multiplicity, and Entropy (Multiplicity, eq 4.20; Entropy, eqs 4.25-4.26)
The Einstein Solid (eqs 5.37-5.40)

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.aha: Quanta flow from the small solid holding 40 quanta into the large solid that already holds 60, and stop when both have about one quantum per oscillator: equilibrium is equal temperature, not equal energy.

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.title: The Free Energy of a Two-Level System

The Boltzmann Factor and the Partition Function (degenerate levels contribute w e^(−βE))

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.aha: At k_BT = 0.2ε a 1000-fold excited level holds 87 % of the probability even though each of its states is e^−5 less likely, because F falls as −TS drops faster than Ē rises; the crossover sits at k_BT = ε/ln w.

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.title: Warming a Crystal of Two-Level Systems

notes.title: Two-Level Systems and Paramagnetism (The Two-Level System, eqs 5.29-5.31, Fig 34 Schottky anomaly)

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.aha: The same +0.1 warming step lights 3 sites when cold, 18 near k_BT ≈ 0.45Δ and only 2 when hot, so the heat capacity peaks (0.439 Nk_B at k_BT = 0.417Δ) and the upper level never passes half.

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.title: Which Way a Reaction Runs — Gibbs Function against Extent of Reaction for A₂ ⇌ 2A

thermal and statistical physics/courses/.aha: Even with a favourable Δφ < 0, a mixture released at ξ = 0.98 runs backwards to ξ_e = 0.805, because the slope is k_BT ln(Q/K), not Δφ alone.

waves and acoustics/courses/wv-antireson.aha: Between the two resonances the driven block stands dead still while the other block swings in antiphase with exactly F0/κc, so the coupling spring cancels the drive.

waves and acoustics/courses/wv-coupled-p.title: Energy Exchange between Coupled Pendulums

waves and acoustics/courses/wv-coupled-p.aha: Halving the spring doubles the transfer time, and making one pendulum just 5% longer caps the transfer at about half the energy yet makes it turn back sooner.

waves and acoustics/courses/wv-duct-mode.title: Modes of a Rectangular Duct

waves and acoustics/courses/wv-end-loads.title: Loads at the End of a String

waves and acoustics/courses/wv-evanescen.title: A Wave Meeting a Stretch of String on Springs

waves and acoustics/courses/wv-fluid-lay.title: Layers of Fluid in a Plane Sound Wave

Plane and Spherical Sound Waves (u = p/ρ0c, Fig. 90)

waves and acoustics/courses/wv-launched-.title: Releasing and Launching a Pulse on a String

waves and acoustics/courses/wv-loaded-mo.title: The Normal Modes of a Loaded String

The Continuum Limit

waves and acoustics/courses/wv-loudspeak.title: A Row of Loudspeakers

notes.title: Interference, Coherence, and Diffraction (A Row of Sources, Eqs. 4.68-4.71, Figs. 71-72)

waves and acoustics/courses/wv-packet-sp.title: Two Wave Packets on an Elastic Foundation

notes.title: Wave Packets (spreading of a Gaussian packet, Eq. 5.34; doubling time ∝ σ²)

waves and acoustics/courses/wv-packet-sp.topic: Two Gaussian packets of chosen widths on a string on an elastic foundation (or plain string); envelopes, grey snapshots and σ(t) plot.

waves and acoustics/courses/wv-phase-gro.title: A Group of Waves on a String

notes.title: Dispersion, Phase Velocity, and Group Velocity (Group Velocity, Fig. 82-83; stiff string)

waves and acoustics/courses/wv-phase-gro.topic: Two-wave group on a string on an elastic foundation, a plain string and a stiff string; marked crest vs group maximum, with an omega(k) inset showing chord slope and tangent slope.

waves and acoustics/courses/wv-plucked-s.title: A String Plucked at a Point

notes.title: The Continuum Limit - A String Plucked at a Point (Fig. 26)
